description: Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a beloved Indian curry featuring succulent chicken pieces simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Its signature mild sweetness and aromatic spices create an irresistible flavor profile. This dish offers a comforting and luxurious culinary experience perfect for any meal.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1/2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 tsp red chili powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute the onions until they turn translucent and light golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1/2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, remaining 1/2 tsp red chili powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala, cumin powder, coriander powder, and salt to taste. Add the soaked cashews and 1/2 cup of water. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf) if desired, though they can also be blended. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky sauce, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan, discarding any solids.

instructions.title: Finish the Curry
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, crushed Kasoori Methi, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and cook for 1-2 minutes, without boiling, until heated through.

instructions.title: Serve Garnish
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with warm naan bread, roti, or basmati rice for a truly authentic Indian experience.

tips: For the best flavor, allow the chicken to marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight. This tenderizes the chicken and infuses it with spices.
Always use good quality, unsalted butter for the authentic rich taste. Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your spice preference.
To achieve a restaurant-style silky texture, ensure you blend the sauce until absolutely smooth, and straining it through a fine-mesh sieve is crucial.
article:
Unveiling the unparalleled delight of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani, a dish that has captivated hearts and palates worldwide. This iconic Indian delicacy, often hailed as the king of comfort food, is a perfect choice for a satisfying Indian lunch. Its luscious, creamy tomato-based gravy, infused with aromatic spices and tender pieces of chicken, makes it an irresistible culinary experience. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore the vibrant flavors of Indian cuisine, mastering Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a rewarding journey that promises a meal brimming with warmth and rich taste. Get ready to embark on a flavorful adventure as we delve into the secrets behind this beloved dish.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, this dish was serendipitously created by Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant. The story goes that he combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich, tomato-based gravy abundant in butter and cream to prevent it from drying out. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained immense popularity. What distinguishes Murgh Makhani is its smooth, velvety texture and a delicate balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried, before being simmered in a gravy made from tomatoes, cashews, ginger, garlic, and a medley of spices like garam masala and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), all generously enriched with butter and fresh cream. It’s this indulgent combination that makes Butter Chicken a perennial favorite and a staple on Indian restaurant menus globally, especially for lunch.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani requires a thoughtful selection of fresh ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to create this culinary marvel:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1.5 lbs (about 700g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp salt
*   1 tbsp lemon juice

For the Gravy:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (28 oz / 794g) crushed tomatoes or 4-5 ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, then drained)
*   1 tsp cumin powder
*   1 tsp coriander powder
*   1 tsp red chili powder (adjust to your spice preference)
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 tsp sugar (or to taste, balances the tanginess)
*   1/2 tsp salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus extra for garnish)
*   1/4 cup water (or chicken broth, as needed for consistency)

For Garnish:
*   Fresh coriander leaves, chopped
*   A swirl of heavy cream

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these detailed steps to prepare an authentic and mouth-watering Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan (cook in batches if necessary). Cook for 5-7 minutes on each side until lightly charred and cooked through. Remove the chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or pureed fresh tomatoes), soaked cashews, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, and garam masala. Mix well and bring to a simmer. Cover the pan and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the oil starts to separate.
5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing down to extract all the liquid.
6.  **Simmer the Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the crushed kasuri methi, sugar, and salt. Stir well. Add the cooked chicken pieces and 1/4 cup water (or broth) if the gravy is too thick.
7.  **Finish with Cream:** Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the gravy. Stir in the heavy cream. Cook for just 1-2 minutes more, ensuring the cream is heated through but not boiled vigorously, as this can cause it to split. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
8.  **Garnish and Serve:** Ladle the hot Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves and a swirl of extra heavy cream.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination truly elevates the dish.
*   **Char the Chicken:** While you might not have a tandoor, giving your chicken a good sear or even broiling it for a few minutes after cooking adds a smoky, charred flavor that mimics traditional tandoori chicken, a hallmark of authentic Butter Chicken.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is crucial for that signature velvety texture. If you don't have a high-powered blender, sieving the gravy after blending will remove any remaining fibrous bits.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality unsalted butter and fresh, full-fat heavy cream for the richest flavor and texture. Kashmiri red chili powder is recommended for its vibrant color without excessive heat.
*   **Don't Skip Kasuri Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is essential to Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance Flavors:** The perfect Butter Chicken strikes a balance between sweet, tangy, and savory. Adjust sugar and salt to your preference, tasting as you go. A touch of lemon juice at the end can brighten the flavors.
*   **Resting Time:** Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a complete meal in itself, but its rich gravy pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. For a truly authentic Indian lunch experience, consider these serving suggestions:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy naan bread, especially garlic naan or butter naan, is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the creamy gravy. Roti, chapati, or paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Aromatic basmati rice, either plain steamed or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice), provides a delightful contrast to the richness of the curry and helps soak up the flavors.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita (yogurt with grated cucumber and mild spices) or a simple plain yogurt helps balance the richness and spiciness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Salad:** A fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette can add a refreshing crunch and cut through the richness.
*   **Pickles and Chutneys:** A side of Indian pickles (achar) or mango chutney can add an extra layer of tangy or sweet-spicy flavor, complementing the main dish beautifully.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is a masterpiece, there are several ways to adapt it to different dietary needs or preferences without sacrificing flavor:

*   **Vegetarian Options:**
    *   **Paneer Makhani:** Substitute the chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese). Marinate the paneer lightly and pan-fry until golden before adding to the gravy.
    *   **Tofu Makhani:** For a vegan option, use firm or extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into cubes. Marinate and pan-fry as you would chicken.
    *   **Mixed Vegetable Makhani:** Incorporate a medley of vegetables like cauliflower, potatoes, peas, and carrots for a hearty vegetarian version.
*   **Dairy-Free/Vegan:**
    *   Replace butter with a good quality vegan butter.
    *   Substitute heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream (made by blending soaked cashews with water). Ensure your yogurt for marination is also plant-based.
*   **Spicier Version:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder in both the marinade and the gravy, or add finely chopped green chilies to the gravy base.
*   **Healthier Twist:**
    *   Use lean chicken breast instead of thighs.
    *   Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use low-fat versions.
    *   Increase the proportion of tomatoes in the gravy.
*   **Nut Substitutions:** If you have a cashew allergy, blanched almonds or sunflower seeds can be used as a substitute to provide thickness and richness to the gravy. Soak them similarly before blending.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani stands as a testament to the rich tapestry of Indian culinary traditions, offering a symphony of flavors that is both comforting and exhilarating. Its universal appeal makes it a perfect choice for any occasion, especially a satisfying Indian lunch. With these detailed instructions and tips, you are now equipped to recreate this legendary dish in your own kitchen. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in every spoonful of this truly magnificent curry.
